source_route: Raw post; Full text Table 3. Each of seven randomized parallel groups had n=8. Primary broad estimate combines all six active arms before comparison with the single shared sham: active n=48, post DMS RCS=.4200, pooled SD=.10708; sham n=8, post=.3900, SD=.1100. Pre values: active=.37667, pooled SD=.09855; sham=.3900, SD=.1400. Composite calculated using standard within-plus-between-arm sums of squares. This avoids selective inclusion of favorable arms and double counting the shared sham. Post-score Hedges g is used because change-score SDs and exact group×time tests were not reported.
Raw post; Table 3 exact mean±SD; LLLT vs CON. Prespecified primary Hwang cognitive endpoint.

F-derived interaction; Full text reports group×time F(1,28)=4.48, p=.043. Hedges g derived from signed change contrast using t=√F and equal n=15/arm; sign set from reported greater RT decrease with active PBM. Within-active d=.55 is not used for pooling.

Raw change; Tables 1, 3 and 4. Analyzed n=14 active, n=13 placebo. Change SDs converted from reported SE: active .11×√14=.4116; placebo .15×√13=.5408. Baseline imbalance supports change-score route. Composite selected as primary.

t-derived independent post; Full text: active n=18, control n=15. Baseline corrected to active A′ 0.91±0.05 and control 0.92±0.04. Exact post between-group t(31)=−0.279, p=.78 converted to Hedges g. Selected primary cognition outcome under accuracy-over-RT rule. No figure digitization required.

t-derived paired; Full text, Results §§3.1–3.3; Figs. 3–4. Valid analyzed sample: L1 n=28 and L2 n=28 (total paired n=56). Study-level sentence-processing P (lower=better): sham 2556.09±733.21 ms; active 2343.36±674.59 ms. Mixed repeated-measures stimulation effect F(1,54)=10.931, p=.002, partial eta²=.168; signed t-equivalent=-sqrt(F)=-3.3062 used for paired Hedges g, with direction multiplier -1. No stimulation×group interaction: F(1,54)=0.809, p=.372. Sensitivity/subgroup data retained: L1 sham 2104.35±442.42, active 1948.92±395.06, t(27)=2.085, d=.394, p=.047; L2 sham 3009.46±688.90, active 2737.80±669.50, t(27)=2.575, d=.487, p=.016. Verbal WM stimulation F(1,54)=1.835,p=.181; visual WM F(1,54)=0.016,p=.899. Fig. 4 correlations are behavioral moderators, not EEG links.

study: Zhao C et al. 2022 — visual WM/CDA (Sci Adv)
source_route: Reported effect—within-paper aggregate; Full text Results; Figs. 1 and 6. Primary cognition estimate aggregates two independent 1064-nm/right-PFC crossover samples: Exp.1 orientation K, n=23, t(22)=2.841,p=.009, reported d=.568, t-derived g=.5720,var=.04764, mean active−sham change=.186±.065; Exp.2 color K, n=18, t(17)=2.760,p=.013, reported d=.651, t-derived g=.6214,var=.06142, change=.188±.051. Fixed within-paper aggregate g=.5936,var=.02683. Experiments 3 (852 nm right PFC,n=19) and 4 (1064 nm left PFC,n=19) are parameter-control sensitivity evidence and are not included in this primary efficacy estimate. QC flag: the printed main-effect partial η²=.925 is incompatible with F(1,40)=13.436, and Exp.4 repeats t/d values that conflict with its stated change; verify supplement/author data before pooling Exp.3–4.

Raw change; Exact means from Results/Fig. 3. Change SDactive=(14.3/2.3)×√9=18.652; change SDcontrol=(2.1/0.3)×√9=21.000. Estimates are approximate because reported t values are rounded. Fig. 3 error bars are SE; no digitization used. Total score is the selected primary Chan MCI outcome.

F-derived change-score SMD; Prespecified Barrett study-level primary under the accuracy-over-RT rule. Full text explicitly reports treatment×pre/post interaction F(1,36)=5.513 with randomized n=20/arm. Pooling-ready; raw group data are optional rather than required.

Raw post; Full text Table 2/results. Active n=20, post MMSE 24.6±3.8; sham n=20, 25.1±4.2. ANCOVA adjusted mean difference -0.5 (95% CI -2.8 to 1.8), p=.670. Clean transcranial-only randomized sham-controlled null result; retain in primary cognition model.

F-derived adjusted independent-groups SMD; Table 3 is source of record: ANCOVA-adjusted RAT F=5.74, p=.020, partial eta²=.098. Abstract reports F=6.15, p=.016; discrepancy flagged. Randomized N=56 (28/arm) retained despite a participant-table count inconsistency. Hedges g derived from adjusted F; positive favors tPBM.

F-derived group×time SMD; Full text Fig. 4 reports MMSE group×time F(1,40)=20, p<.001 in a randomized 21/arm trial. For a 2-group×2-time interaction, t=sqrt(F)=4.472; Hedges g derived from the signed between-group difference in change with small-sample correction. This replaces the earlier direct partial-eta-squared conversion. Primary cognition effect; no author data needed.

Independent post-treatment SMD; Primary K-MoCA outcome. Table 3: week 13 active 25.92±2.84 vs sham 20.92±5.12, n=13/arm; mean difference 5.00 [1.65,8.35], p=.005. Baseline 21.62±3.69 vs 19.62±4.57; ANCOVA week-13 p=.002 corroborates the treatment difference. Randomized, concealed, double-blind sham-controlled; all 26 completed. Raw randomized post-score SMD used for consistency with existing master hierarchy.

Independent change-score SMD from reported week-2 change means±SDs; Kheradmand A, Donboli S, Taheri Tanjani P, et al. 2022. Therapeutic Effects of Low-Level Laser Therapy on Cognitive Symptoms of Patients with Dementia: A Double-Blinded Randomized Clinical Trial. doi:10.1089/photob.2021.0135. n=32 randomized equally; MMSE change at week 2: active 2.31±1.81 vs sham 0.13±0.96. Week 2 selected as primary; week-8 follow-up retained secondary. Distinct from Kheradmand et al. 2022 schizophrenia RCT, which remains excluded under the psychiatric-population criterion.

Paired SMD from raw post values using r=.50; sensitivity r=.20/.80; Correctly mapped to Lee T-L et al. 2025, Transcranial photobiomodulation improves cognitive function, post-concussion, and PTSD symptoms in mild traumatic brain injury, J Neurotrauma 42:1695-1707, doi:10.1089/neu.2025.0048. These values were previously disabled only because they were assigned to the wrong Lee 2025 citation. This is an independent randomized transcranial-only neurological cohort. VWM span selected without regard to significance; span-9 RT and HKLLT remain secondary dependent outcomes.

t-derived independent-groups SMD; n=22/22 accepted from extraction/Table 1; effect direction reoriented so positive favors tPBM; Extraction form/Table 1 reports N=88 randomized, 22/group. Per reviewer decision on 2026-08-25, use n=22 for the tPBM-alone and dual-sham arms despite two TMS-related withdrawals elsewhere in the four-arm trial. Direct tPBM-alone vs dual-sham contrast: t=-2.566, p=.014; df=42 implied by n1+n0-2. Hedges g computed from |t|×sqrt(1/22+1/22), small-sample corrected; sign oriented positive for tPBM benefit. Combined TMS+tPBM arm excluded from this effect.

Independent change-score SMD from published mean changes and Figure 4B SDs digitized from supplied high-resolution figure; Full text verified 2026-08-25. Randomized n=93 (47 tPBM/46 placebo); principal cognition dataset n=76, using n=40 tPBM and n=36 placebo as stated in abstract, Results, Table 2, and Fig. 4 caption. Baseline MoCA 19.3±3.3 vs 18.5±3.8. Day-60 changes: +3.20 vs +1.97; p=.0002. Fig. 4B explicitly plots mean±SD; high-resolution digitization gives SDchange≈1.268 tPBM and 1.506 placebo. Hedges g=.87886, var=.057997. Note: CONSORT Fig. 3 visually shows placebo analyzed n=37 with one biochemical exclusion, but the cognition figure/text consistently specify total n=76 and placebo n=36; n=40/36 used for meta-analysis.

Independent-groups change-score SMD from full-text n=40/40; Hedges correction J=.9903537; variance J²[(n1+n0)/(n1n0)+d²/(2df)].; Full-text ILL audit 2026-08-27. 80 randomized 1:1 (40/40). No post-randomization losses are reported; Figure 1/adherence reporting is consistent with the 40/40 FAS, though attrition reporting is not CONSORT-detailed. Primary week-13 MoCA-K change +3.87±2.51 active vs -0.74±2.85 sham. Block randomization by independent statistician; double-blind identical devices; independent occupational-therapist assessment. Sham delivers ~1/50 active output and remains core-eligible under locked comparator rule. Promote provisional study to confirmed core; final cognition k=23.

Independent change-score SMD from Figure 3 participant-level MMSE pairs; pooled change-score SD; Hedges small-sample correction J=0.88889; sampling variance J²[(n1+n0)/(n1n0)+d²/(2df)]; Figure 3 independently re-audited 2026-08-25. Active MMSE pairs: 14→16, 17→19, 18→20, 19→19, 23→25, 23→20; placebo: 11→13, 16→15, 28→28. Changes active [2,2,2,0,2,-3], placebo [2,-1,0]. Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled transcranial-only trial meets primary cognition eligibility. Major concerns: n=9 completers from 11 enrolled, unclear randomization/concealment/sham implementation, selective/multiple outcome reporting, industry/patent conflicts. Include in core; exclude in digitized-estimate and major-RoB sensitivities. qEEG remains narrative only.

Paired standardized mean difference using protocol r=.50; SDdiff=sqrt(SDactive²+SDsham²−2r·SDactive·SDsham); Hedges correction J(df=54); paired-effect sampling variance; Supplementary Table A1 resolves the preferred endpoint: active 3-back accuracy 0.63±0.17 vs sham 0.56±0.18, n=55 paired. Accuracy was the article's main/sample-size-planning outcome. Within-participant correlation is not reported, so protocol v1.1 central r=.50 is used with r=.20/.80 sensitivity rows. Yang is the sole core representative of the potentially overlapping Xuanwu older-adult program; Qu 2022 remains fixed-order sensitivity and Hu 2023 mechanistic/companion, so they are not co-counted as independent primary studies.

Independent-groups SMD derived from group×time F: t=sqrt(F); d=t*sqrt(1/n_active+1/n_sham); Hedges small-sample correction; variance=(n1+n0)/(n1*n0)+g²/[2(n1+n0−2)]; Full-text audit 2026-08-25. Simple random allocation, n=17/arm, all participants completed with no missing data. Efficiency score is identified as the main attentional parameter. Body reports group×time F(1,30)=10.68, p=.003; abstract reports p=.004. Sham delivered ~1/12 cumulative active energy. Locked comparator rule treats nonzero-dose shams as core-eligible when all other core criteria are met.

Reported between-group Cohen d transformed to Hedges g using small-sample correction J=1-3/[4(n1+n0)-9]; variance=(n1+n0)/(n1*n0)+g²/[2(n1+n0−2)]; Full-text audit 2026-08-25. CPT correct rejections is explicitly the primary behavioral outcome. Stage 1 diagnosis×treatment interaction F(1,219)=4.924, p=.028; ADHD subgroup active vs sham F(1,25)=6.71, p=.017, reported d=.93 and 51% improvement. Stage 1 ADHD cells: active n=15, sham n=12. Use one study-level Salehpour contribution; Stage 2 is supportive and not a second k.

study: Zhao X et al. 2022 — SCD sleep/cognition (JAD)
source_route: Compute SDchange within each arm from paired t: SDchange=|mean change|×sqrt(n)/|t|; calculate independent-groups change-score SMD, reverse direction because lower RT=better, then Hedges correction J=0.9865471. Chosen 2-back RT because 2-back is the authors' highlighted WM load and accuracy lacks participant-level variance.; Full-text + journal supplement audit 2026-08-26. 68 randomized 34/34; 58 completed (32 active/26 sham), with differential attrition. Main Table 3 ACC counts are pooled trials, not participants, and post-only RT t values do not reconcile with participant n/means/SDs. Supplementary Tables 1-2 provide within-arm pre/post RT means, SDs, and paired t values, allowing change-SD reconstruction. Baseline cognitive/n-back imbalance makes controlled change preferable. Count as a distinct study from Chenguang Zhao et al. 2022 Science Advances; flag possible Xuanwu/SILCODE program overlap with Yang 2025 for sensitivity because shared infrastructure/authors exist but no participant reuse is reported.
